input.response: The beaches around Sarandë are some of Albania's finest. Ksamil is the top pick — four small islands sit just offshore, the water is a vivid turquoise, and you can rent a pedal boat to reach them for about 500 ALL. The town itself has plenty of seafood restaurants along the promenade. Aim to arrive before 10 AM in July and August to secure a spot on the sand.

input.response: Berat Castle (Kalaja e Beratit) sits on a rocky hill above the White City and dates to the 4th century BC, though most of the current walls are Byzantine and Ottoman. Inside the walls is a living neighbourhood — families still reside there year-round. The Church of the Holy Trinity and Onufri National Museum are both worth the climb. Entry to the castle grounds is free; the Onufri Museum charges a small fee.

_note: Historical and practical travel info, grounded in Albania content

input.response: The most common international gateway is Tirana International Airport (TIA). Many visitors fly via Athens, Rome, or Vienna and connect onward. From Athens you can also take the ferry from Igoumenitsa to Sarandë — a scenic three-hour crossing that lands you right on the Albanian Riviera.

input.response: A few practical notes before you arrive: Albania uses the Albanian lek (ALL); euros are widely accepted in tourist areas but you'll get better rates paying in lek. A local SIM from ONE Telecommunications or Vodafone Albania costs around 500 ALL with a data bundle. If you're driving, the roads in the south (especially the Llogara Pass) are scenic but narrow — an SUV or crossover handles them more comfortably than a small hatchback.
